title: Core: Fix manual zoom input field UX
body:
## What I did

Instead of having the `%` "unit" as part of the input value, keep just the number as the input value and show the unit as a non-selectable, non-editable suffix. This avoids parsing issues, specifically when a number is appended after the unit (e.g. `100%1`), which is syntactically invalid.

**Mask overlay is misaligned with input text due to missing padding compensation.**

The `Mask` is positioned at `left: 0` but the input text starts at `left: 10px` due to the input's `padding: '6px 10px'` defined in styles.ts. The hidden span inside the Mask will measure the value text from position 0, causing the suffix to appear 10px to the left of where it should be.

Adjust the Mask's `left` position to match the input's left padding:

<details>
<summary>💡 Suggested fix</summary>

```diff
 const Mask = styled.div({
   position: 'absolute',
-  left: 0,
+  left: 10,
   right: 0,
   top: 0,
   bottom: 0,
   display: 'flex',
   alignItems: 'center',
   pointerEvents: 'none',
   overflow: 'hidden',
   color: 'inherit',
   'span:first-of-type': {
     opacity: 0,
   },
 });
```

</details>

For better maintainability, consider extracting the padding as a constant or CSS variable to avoid hardcoding values.

comments.body:
_⚠️ Potential issue_ | _🔴 Critical_

**Critical: Operator precedence bug causes incorrect unit stripping.**

The condition `unit === fixedUnit || baseUnit` is evaluated as `((unit === fixedUnit) || baseUnit)` due to operator precedence. Since `baseUnit` defaults to `fixedUnit` (a truthy string like `"%"`), the condition is always `true` when a unit is configured, causing the unit to be stripped from the display value regardless of what the parsed unit actually is.

This means if a user types `100px` but `fixedUnit` is `%`, the display would incorrectly show `100` instead of `100px`.


<details>
<summary>🐛 Proposed fix</summary>

```diff
-      setInputValue(`${number}${unit === fixedUnit || baseUnit ? '' : unit}`);
+      setInputValue(`${number}${(unit === fixedUnit || unit === baseUnit) ? '' : unit}`);
```

</details>

<!-- suggestion_start -->

<details>
<summary>📝 Committable suggestion</summary>

> ‼️ **IMPORTANT**
> Carefully review the code before committing. Ensure that it accurately replaces the highlighted code, contains no missing lines, and has no issues with indentation. Thoroughly test & benchmark the code to ensure it meets the requirements.

```suggestion
        setInputValue(`${number}${(unit === fixedUnit || unit === baseUnit) ? '' : unit}`);
```

</details>

<!-- suggestion_end -->

<details>
<summary>🤖 Prompt for AI Agents</summary>

```
In `@code/core/src/manager/components/preview/NumericInput.tsx` at line 113, The
displayed value is stripping units due to wrong operator precedence in
NumericInput where setInputValue uses `unit === fixedUnit || baseUnit`; change
that condition to explicitly compare the parsed unit against both values (e.g.,
`unit === fixedUnit || unit === baseUnit`) so the ternary only strips the unit
when the parsed unit matches one of those, then update the setInputValue call
accordingly inside the NumericInput component.
```
